character_facts: Aghnar has lost an arm and is still able to stand and fight.
Aghnar is highly stoic and speaks as though spiritual integrity matters more to him than bodily harm.
Oda is close enough to assist Aghnar medically or physically and is deeply concerned for him.
The elders speak collectively and act together in opposition to a person they call a traitor.

dialogue_meaning: Oda is urgently trying to treat or warn Aghnar about his life-threatening injury.
Aghnar minimizes his physical suffering and emphasizes endurance and morale.
Aghnar frames inner resolve or spirit as something enemies cannot damage.
The elders reject the idea that their power comes entirely from Jejoh.
The elders identify someone as a traitor and decide to use their last reserves of power to destroy that person.

Aghnar says only the stump hurts and insists the rest of him is fine.
Aghnar declares that his spirit cannot be wounded even if his body is injured.
Aghnar raises a firearm and shoots toward an off-panel target.
A group of elders reveals itself and states that it has power independent of Jejoh.
The elders threaten to spend their remaining energy to exterminate the 'traitor.'
A powerful energy blast erupts and hurls or strikes Aghnar while Oda calls his name.

visual_summary: In a chaotic interior battlefield littered with bodies, Oda tends to the badly wounded Aghnar, whose arm has been severed at the stump. Aghnar remains defiant despite heavy blood loss, draws a gun, and fires at an unseen opponent while Oda recoils behind him. Nearby, shadowy hooded elders declare that they are not wholly dependent on Jejoh and will use their own power against a traitor. A bright purple-white blast then strikes or throws Aghnar backward as Oda cries out to him.
